note: Experiment 133b. Every closed kamp-us/phoenix ticket that ever carried `status:needs-info`, read from every issue's label events on 2026-10-24: 70 closed, one of them the triage self-test #44, left out as in 133. That leaves 69: the 15 that 133 drew, the other 36 of 133's 51, and 18 filed from #7852 on that 133's count never reached (`late`). Each ticket was read by hand from its first body, triage's comments and what came after, before any sort answer was seen. The fields follow 133's note. `end`: built (the asked-for work was done, mostly by a merged PR), no_answer, no (closed as not worth doing), duplicate (closed as a duplicate or as covered by another ticket), or ruled (the ticket asked an owner for a call, the call was made, nothing was left to build). `asked`: what the label waited on. `to`: who the ask was put to. `answered`: someone gave it; a batch sweep that closed stale tickets is not an answer. `who`: what the label waited on, by 133's own wording: the filer, the code (or the GitHub API), an owner's ruling on a real question, or an owner's permission only, where triage already knew its answer and a rule kept it from acting (no agent footer, no close authority in that run, no open milestone at that priority). `from`: where the fact the park turned on sat: issues (the board: a duplicate, a covering ticket, a standing ruling), code (source, CI, git or the API), owner, filer, or none (nothing beyond the ticket's text and a home). `changed`: that fact moved the end away from what the ticket's own text asks for (a refuted premise, or a ruling against it); later events that had nothing to do with the park, such as a product removed or a batch sweep, do not count. `of`: the tickets a duplicate or covered ticket belonged to, when the record names them. `why` is a few words.

recheckNote: The blind re-read of 133's 15. A fresh agent that had not seen 133's files classified them from the tickets alone, with 133's field words (`blind`). Then 133's labels were opened and every disagreement was read again by hand. The labels here are the result, by the same rules as `needsInfo`; 133's own labels stay in `133-truth.json`. `to`, `answered` and `of` were added last, from each ticket's park comment and close, by the same rules; the blind reader was not asked for them.
